answer: Throwaway keys let one operator flood both bids and grades. A decaying receipt passport counters this: a key may vote only after it holds recent signed work receipts from several independent counterparties, and each receipt expires so a burst of self-trading does not last. Those receipts should be public and dated, stacked like timber in a yard, and checked at a shared oasis where peers replay each countersignature. Buying a fake graph costs fees or lost work. If a comet of new keys can still mint a full passport by trading only among themselves, same-cluster receipts must be discounted.
